hide_of_nemean_lion.name: Hide of the Nemean Lion
hide_of_nemean_lion.unidentified_name: a rough amber pelt of unnatural density
hide_of_nemean_lion.lore: Heracles for his first Labour was sent against the Nemean Lion, and all the hardship of it was that no blade could cut the beast. His arrows sprang back from the hide and his club broke upon its skull, so at last he cornered it in its cave and strangled it, and found that nothing but one of its own claws would skin it. He wore the pelt all his life with the jaws above his head. Steel slides from it still, though a blow that is hard enough will bruise the one within.
hide_of_nemean_lion.special: Halves every cut, stab and blow a creature without magic lands on you.

carapace_of_the_hydra.name: Carapace of the Hydra
carapace_of_the_hydra.unidentified_name: a greenish scaled vest that smells faintly of venom
carapace_of_the_hydra.lore: For every head that was hewn from the Hydra of Lerna two grew again, until Iolaus brought a torch and seared each stump. Heracles dipped his arrows in its gall, and the venom outlived the monster, for it wounded the centaur Chiron past all healing and killed Nessus, and through the robe that Nessus steeped in his own blood it killed Heracles at the last. The scales took no hurt from the poison they covered, and whatever bites the one who wears them learns to its sorrow what lay beneath.
carapace_of_the_hydra.special: A monster that poisons you has a 40% chance of being poisoned itself.

panoply_of_hephaestus.name: Panoply of Hephaestus
panoply_of_hephaestus.unidentified_name: a suit of armour of inhuman precision
panoply_of_hephaestus.lore: Hephaestus was born lame, and for that his mother Hera cast him down from Olympus into the sea, where the nymph Thetis hid him nine years. Yet he returned as the one god whom the others could not spare, for he built handmaids of gold that could speak and carry, the bronze giant Talos who guarded Crete, and a throne from which Hera could not rise again. This harness is the work of his own bench, and any smith who has handled it finds that his hammer strikes truer afterward.
panoply_of_hephaestus.special: While it is worn, your weapon can be enchanted one step higher.

dragon_mail_of_sigurd.name: Dragon-Sewn Mail of Sigurd
dragon_mail_of_sigurd.unidentified_name: a shirt of scale-linked rings with a faint iridescence
dragon_mail_of_sigurd.lore: In the track by which the dragon Fafnir went down to the water, Sigurd dug a pit, and he thrust upward as the worm crawled over him. The German poem, which calls him Siegfried, tells also that he bathed in the blood and his skin grew hard as horn, save in the one place where a linden leaf had clung between his shoulder blades. His wife sewed a little cross on his tunic to show a friend where he must be guarded, and Hagen read that mark and thrust a spear through it.

breastplate_of_joan.name: Breastplate of Joan of Arc
breastplate_of_joan.unidentified_name: a plain breastplate of bare polished steel, cut small
breastplate_of_joan.lore: Joan was seventeen when she told the Dauphin that God had sent her to raise the siege of Orleans, and Charles had a harness made for her at Tours of plain polished steel, the kind that armourers called white. At Orleans an arrow pierced her above the breast, but she had it drawn and was at the wall again that evening, and the English fort fell. Though her enemies burned her at Rouen in 1431, the Church struck down their judgment in 1456, and in 1920 it named her among the saints.
breastplate_of_joan.special: Once a floor, a blow that would kill you leaves you at 1 health. Blessed while worn.

lorica_hamata_of_caesar.name: Lorica of Caesar
lorica_hamata_of_caesar.unidentified_name: a fine ring-mail shirt with a faded red hem
lorica_hamata_of_caesar.lore: Through eight years in Gaul this lorica hamata, the ringed mail of the legions, went with the armies of Julius Caesar. But on the Ides of March he wore no armour to the Senate, for he had dismissed his Spanish bodyguard and would not heed the soothsayer Spurinna, and the conspirators stabbed him twenty-three times. The physician Antistius judged that the second wound alone, the one in the chest, was mortal. The mail remembers that day when it was left at home, and it takes vengeance upon the first blade that finds it.
lorica_hamata_of_caesar.special: The first monster to wound you is marked: you deal half again as much damage to it.

orichalcum_breastplate.name: Orichalcum Breastplate
orichalcum_breastplate.unidentified_name: a chest-piece of reddish-gold metal that vibrates faintly
orichalcum_breastplate.lore: The kings of Atlantis, as Plato relates in the Critias, dug orichalcum out of the earth in every part of their island and held gold alone more precious. They sheathed the wall of their inner citadel with it so that it flashed red as fire, until in a single day and night the sea took the island. Scholars suppose that the metal was some kind of brass, yet no brass was ever heard to hum as this breastplate does, and at the height of each slow beat it turns blows aside.
orichalcum_breastplate.special: Now and then it hums, and for that moment you are Shielded.

helm_of_hades.name: Helm of Darkness
helm_of_hades.unidentified_name: a dark helm that the eye keeps sliding away from
helm_of_hades.lore: Before the war with the Titans the Cyclopes made three gifts for the sons of Cronus: the thunderbolt for Zeus, the trident for Poseidon, and for Hades a cap that hid its wearer from every eye. Perseus wore it when he fled the Gorgon's sisters, and Athena put it on at Troy, so that Ares should not see who guided the spear into his belly. It can hide a man even from the gods, and the dead, being the subjects of its owner, look straight through whoever has it on.

helm_of_achilles.name: Helm of Achilles
helm_of_achilles.unidentified_name: a four-ridged helm with a crest of golden hair
helm_of_achilles.lore: After Hector had stripped the first armour of Achilles from the body of Patroclus, Thetis went by night to Hephaestus, and at dawn she bore down new arms, with a helmet four times ridged and crested with gold. Homer tells that when she laid them before her son they rang aloud, and the Myrmidons trembled and would not look, but Achilles looked and his anger grew. The helm has kept that voice, and at every new threshold it rings out to make the enemy tremble likewise.
helm_of_achilles.special: Each monster that first sees you has a 40% chance of fleeing in fear.

great_helm_of_galahad.name: Great Helm of Galahad
great_helm_of_galahad.unidentified_name: a white great helm with a small red cross on the cheek
great_helm_of_galahad.lore: Galahad came to Camelot without a shield and sat in the Siege Perilous, which was the ruin of every unworthy knight, and took no harm from it. At a white abbey he received the shield that had been kept for him, white, with a red cross which the son of Joseph of Arimathea had drawn centuries before in his own blood. He alone looked into the Grail, and in that hour he prayed that he might die. Nothing foul will cling to what he wore, and curses fall away from the wearer's gear as frost falls from a window.
great_helm_of_galahad.special: Lifts the curse from everything you wear, and from anything you put on later.

vambraces_of_achilles.name: Vambraces of Achilles
vambraces_of_achilles.unidentified_name: a pair of bronze arm-guards worked with tiny farm scenes
vambraces_of_achilles.lore: Among the arms that Hephaestus wrought for Achilles, Homer names a shield, a corselet brighter than fire, a helmet, and greaves of tin. Upon the shield the god set no battles of heroes, but two cities, a wedding, a lawsuit, ploughmen, reapers, a vineyard and a dancing floor, with the river Ocean around the rim. These arm-guards are worked by the same hand with the same quiet scenes, and they give rest to one who wears them on holy ground, as though the smith wished his soldier to remember what the fighting was for.
vambraces_of_achilles.special: Standing on an altar restores 2 mana and 2 stamina a turn.

gauntlets_of_mars.name: Gauntlets of Mars
gauntlets_of_mars.unidentified_name: a pair of iron gauntlets engraved with wolf heads
gauntlets_of_mars.lore: Though the Greeks had only fear for Ares, the Romans loved Mars, the father of Romulus, who was a god of fields and boundaries before ever he was a god of war. The farmers prayed him to keep blight from the wheat, and each March his priests, the Salii, danced through the city with the sacred shields, and when they had finished, the season of campaigns began. The wolf was his beast. These gauntlets are best contented when they hold a line, be it a gate, a doorway or the edge of a field.
gauntlets_of_mars.special: Armor improves by 1 while you stand beside a door.

greaves_of_hermes.name: Greaves of Hermes
greaves_of_hermes.unidentified_name: a pair of bronze greaves, impossibly light, with wings at the ankle
greaves_of_hermes.lore: Hermes, who stole the cattle of Apollo on the very day of his birth, had need of wings, for he was herald to Zeus, guide of the dead upon the road to Hades, and patron of all travellers, traders and thieves. Where those wings grew the painters of Greece could never agree, for some set them upon his sandals and some upon his hat, and others drew them springing from the ankle itself. These shin-guards of bronze follow that third opinion, and whoever straps them on finds that all the world has slowed.

cloak_of_the_morrigan.name: Cloak of the Morrigan
cloak_of_the_morrigan.unidentified_name: a dark feathered cloak that moves without wind
cloak_of_the_morrigan.lore: The Morrigan, Phantom Queen of the Irish, came to battles as a crow and marked those who should fall. When Cu Chulainn refused her love she set upon him at the ford as an eel, a wolf and a hornless heifer, and he wounded her in all three shapes. Afterward he met an old woman milking a cow and blessed her for each of three drinks, and so unknowingly he healed the three wounds that he had given. Yet on his last day a crow alighted on his shoulder, and by that he was marked to fall.

leggings_of_enkidu.name: Leggings of Enkidu
leggings_of_enkidu.unidentified_name: a pair of rough hide leggings stitched with sinew
leggings_of_enkidu.lore: Out of clay that the goddess Aruru pinched off and cast into the wilderness came Enkidu, shaggy as a beast, who ate grass among the gazelles and tore up the traps of the hunters. Shamhat led him to Uruk, where he wrestled in the street with King Gilgamesh until the doorposts shook, and the two became as brothers, though ever afterward the animals fled from him and he grieved for it. These leggings were stitched in his wild years, and beasts that walk beside their wearer are the harder to kill.
leggings_of_enkidu.special: Your pet takes a fifth less damage.

mantle_of_elijah.name: Mantle of Elijah
mantle_of_elijah.unidentified_name: a rough cloak of undyed hair-cloth
mantle_of_elijah.lore: As Elisha ploughed with twelve yoke of oxen Elijah passed by and cast his cloak over him, and Elisha slew the oxen, boiled them over the wood of the plough, fed his neighbours and followed. Years afterward a chariot of fire parted the two, and Elijah went up in a whirlwind and the cloak fell from him. Elisha bore it to the Jordan and struck the water as his master had done, and the river divided. It is a rough and hairy thing that was never dyed, and fire has good reason to respect it.

robe_of_the_magus.name: Robe of the Magus
robe_of_the_magus.unidentified_name: a deep blue robe with silver astronomical diagrams
robe_of_the_magus.lore: The Magi were the priestly scholars of Persia, who read the stars and the dreams of men. Matthew tells that certain of them saw a new star rise and followed it westward to Jerusalem, where they asked King Herod after the child born king of the Jews, and that they found him at Bethlehem and gave him gold, frankincense and myrrh. Being warned of Herod in a dream, they went home by another road. The silver figures upon this robe follow the heavens still, and they reward any mind that will study them.

boots_of_seven_leagues.name: Boots of Seven Leagues
boots_of_seven_leagues.unidentified_name: a pair of worn leather boots that feel ready to move
boots_of_seven_leagues.lore: An ogre once had a pair of fairy boots that went seven leagues at a stride, as Charles Perrault wrote in 1697, and he wearied himself in them hunting seven lost brothers, until he fell asleep upon the very rock where the boys lay hidden. Hop-o'-My-Thumb, the smallest, drew off the boots, which shrank to fit him as fairy boots will, and he ran in them to the king's court and made his fortune as a messenger. They are slow to wear thin, and they are eager yet to be upon the road.
boots_of_seven_leagues.special: Hasted while worn. Once a floor, a power dashes you up to 7 tiles.

brigandine_of_william_wallace.name: Brigandine of Wallace
brigandine_of_william_wallace.unidentified_name: a riveted coat of small iron plates over leather
brigandine_of_william_wallace.lore: William Wallace was a younger son of no great landholder in Scotland. In 1297 he waited with Andrew Moray above Stirling Bridge while an army of the English crossed two riders abreast, and then came down and cut off those who had crossed from those who had not. For years afterward he made war out of the forests and the narrow places, until Edward I had him put to death in London in 1305. This coat of small plates was made for one who chose his ground, and it serves best in a tight passage.
brigandine_of_william_wallace.special: Armor improves by 2 in a corridor or with your back in a corner.

cuirass_of_hannibal.name: Cuirass of Hannibal
cuirass_of_hannibal.unidentified_name: a bronze officer's cuirass embossed with a horse and a palm tree
cuirass_of_hannibal.lore: In 218 BC Hannibal Barca led an army and thirty-seven elephants over the Alps, and for fifteen years he abode in Italy. At Cannae he let his centre bend backward until the Roman host had pressed deep within, and then closed upon it with his African foot on either flank and his horse behind, so that some fifty thousand Romans died in an afternoon. Yet he never took Rome, and Scipio overcame him at Zama. His cuirass is never so strong as when the enemy stands all around its wearer.
cuirass_of_hannibal.special: With three or more enemies beside you, armor improves by 2 and your blows land harder.

aegishjalmr.name: Aegishjalmr
aegishjalmr.unidentified_name: a helm marked on the brow with an eight-armed stave
aegishjalmr.lore: Fafnir the dragon had the Helm of Awe among his hoard, and as he lay dying he told Sigurd that he had worn it against all men and none had dared come near him. Sigurd answered that no helm can save the one who meets a braver man, and with that he took it, together with the gold and the cursed ring. In later books of magic from Iceland it is drawn as a stave of eight branching arms, to be marked upon the brow before a fight, for it is less a helmet than a sign of dread.

winged_sandals_of_hermes.name: Winged Sandals of Hermes
winged_sandals_of_hermes.unidentified_name: a pair of golden sandals with small live wings at the ankles
winged_sandals_of_hermes.lore: Golden and immortal were the sandals of Hermes, and Homer sings that they bore him over the wet sea and the boundless land as swift as the wind. He went in them upon his father's errands, and upon the darker road by which he led the souls of the dead to the river, and certain nymphs lent such a pair to Perseus, who outflew two Gorgons in them. These are the true sandals, and whoever learns them well will no longer be standing where the blow lands.

hermes_sandals_early.name: Hermes's Sandals
hermes_sandals_early.unidentified_name: a pair of plain sandals with small bronze wings riveted on
hermes_sandals_early.lore: A cobbler of mortal race made these in the likeness of the golden sandals that bore Hermes on the wind between Olympus and the underworld, and such a pair a grateful courier would hang upon a temple wall after a safe journey. The wings are of bronze and the leather is good, though common. Yet one brief trick they have from the god of travellers and thieves: in each new place the first archer who takes aim at the wearer will look the wrong way.
hermes_sandals_early.special: The first arrow, bolt or hex aimed at you on each floor misses.

blindfold.name: blindfold
blindfold.lore: To keep from meeting the Gorgon's eyes Perseus had need of a borrowed shield, but a humbler remedy is this strip of heavy black cloth, long enough to be knotted twice. Whoever binds it on sees nothing whatever, and is the safer for it, since there are things in the dark that work their harm through the eyes. The blind learn to read a floor through their boots, and after a while the wearer will know where the nearest footsteps are.
blindfold.special: Blinded while worn, but you feel every monster within 3 tiles, and no gaze can catch you.

trainers_cap.name: Trainer's Cap
trainers_cap.lore: This cap of red and white has seen countless adventures, which have worn it soft and shaped its brim. A warmth and good cheer go out from it to hearten its owner's companion creatures, so that their wounds mend more quickly, and within the brim are written the words 'I choose you.'
trainers_cap.special: Your pet heals faster and gains a level on each new floor you reach.

cow_kings_horns.name: Cow King's Horns
cow_kings_horns.lore: It was long rumoured that there was no such herd and no such king, until at last one adventurer disproved it and pulled these gilded horns from the crowned skull of the Cow King. They lend a bull's temper to whoever wears them, so that the first swing lands before the fight has rightly begun, and upon the left horn is graven a single word: 'Moo.'

cloth_of_penelope.name: Cloth of Penelope
cloth_of_penelope.lore: For twenty years Odysseus was away, and a hundred and eight suitors sat in his hall devouring his herds until his wife should choose among them. Penelope answered that she would choose when she had finished a shroud for old Laertes, and every day she wove at the great loom and every night by torchlight unpicked the work, and so she held them off three years. This robe was cut from that cloth. What is torn in it by day is whole again by morning, and the one who wears it is mended likewise.
cloth_of_penelope.special: You regenerate while it is worn, and faster when badly hurt.

bracers_of_cu_chulainn.name: Bracers of Cu Chulainn
bracers_of_cu_chulainn.unidentified_name: a pair of battle-scarred leather bracers
bracers_of_cu_chulainn.lore: While he was yet the boy Setanta, the guard hound of Culann the smith came at him and he slew it with his bare hands, and then he offered to guard the house himself until a pup should be reared. Thereafter men named him Cu Chulainn, the Hound of Culann. When the battle frenzy took him his body writhed within its skin, one eye sank and the other swelled, and a light rose from his brow. Something of that frenzy remains in these bracers, and every third blow struck by the wearer tears a wound that will not close.
bracers_of_cu_chulainn.special: Every third blow you land opens a bleeding wound.

cloak_of_sun_wukong.name: Cloak of Sun Wukong
cloak_of_sun_wukong.lore: Upon the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit Sun Wukong was hatched from an egg of stone. He wrung from the Dragon Kings of the four seas a coat of golden mail, a cap of phoenix feathers and boots for walking the clouds, he ate the peaches of immortality, and he fought the armies of Heaven to a standstill, until the Buddha shut him beneath a mountain for five hundred years. Seventy-two changes of shape he knew, and none could lay hands on him twice. His cloak has the same habit, and its wearer is seldom quite in the place where he seems to be.
cloak_of_sun_wukong.special: Blows sometimes land where you are not, and every tenth that would hit misses outright.

coat_of_cu_chulainn.name: Coat of Cú Chulainn
coat_of_cu_chulainn.unidentified_name: a blood-red hide coat that is warm to the touch
coat_of_cu_chulainn.lore: When Queen Medb marched upon Ulster to steal the Brown Bull of Cooley, all the men of that land lay in their beds under a curse, save Cu Chulainn alone, who was seventeen. For months he held the fords, meeting by agreement one champion in a day, and this was his war coat. When he was hard pressed the warp-spasm came upon him, and no army could face what he became. The coat remembers, and it wakes when its wearer is near to death: strength floods back and pain fades, but the fury takes its payment from the wearer's life.
coat_of_cu_chulainn.special: Below a quarter health the frenzy takes you: +3 Strength for 10 turns, at 1 health a turn.

babr_e_bayan.name: Babr-e Bayan
babr_e_bayan.unidentified_name: a striped tiger-skin coat, unmarked by any blade
babr_e_bayan.lore: Rostam of Zabul is the great champion of the Persian Book of Kings. He rode upon Rakhsh, the horse that killed a lion while its master slept, and he won through seven trials to slay the White Demon in its cave and set his king free. Over his mail he wore the Babr-e Bayan, a coat of tiger's skin that neither fire nor water nor any weapon could spoil, and in each new place it will wholly refuse the first blow that reaches it.
babr_e_bayan.special: Soaks up the first blow that lands on each floor.

tarnhelm.name: Tarnhelm
tarnhelm.unidentified_name: a dull helm of fine iron mesh
tarnhelm.lore: From the dwarf Alberich, warden of the Nibelung hoard, Siegfried won a cloak of darkness in the old German poem. Wagner made of it a helm of fine mesh, which the smith Mime forged at the bidding of his brother Alberich, and beneath it Alberich walked unseen among his own people with a whip, and in after days the giant Fafner used it to take the shape of a dragon. It can still hide its wearer wholly, though for no more than a few breaths, and then it must rest.
tarnhelm.special: Once a floor, falling below 30% health turns you invisible for 5 turns.

linothorax_of_alexander.name: Linothorax of Alexander
linothorax_of_alexander.unidentified_name: a stiff cuirass of layered white linen
linothorax_of_alexander.lore: Alexander rides bareheaded at the Persian king in the great mosaic that was found at Pompeii, and upon his breast is a corselet of stiffened linen with a Gorgon's face. Plutarch says that at Gaugamela he wore a doubled breastplate of linen from the spoils of Issus. Linen armour was cooler than bronze and lighter for such a march as his phalanx made from Greece to India, and with layers enough it would stop an arrow. A soldier who rests in it upon holy ground is quickly mended.
linothorax_of_alexander.special: Standing on an altar heals 2 health a turn.

coif_of_beowulf.name: Coif of Beowulf
coif_of_beowulf.unidentified_name: a riveted iron coif with small boar figures on the brow
coif_of_beowulf.lore: Since Grendel bore no sword, Beowulf laid his own aside and waited in the darkened hall of Heorot, and there he gripped the monster's arm until it was torn from the shoulder, and the Danes hung it beneath the roof. The poem sings of his helmet, banded by a smith of old and set with boars, that no blade might bite, and in 1939 a ship burial at Sutton Hoo yielded up such a helmet with boars upon the brow. As for this coif, there is nothing that can keep hold of its wearer for long.
coif_of_beowulf.special: Nothing holds you: paralysis, sleep, stuns, ice and strangling grips break at once.

sandals_of_perseus.name: Sandals of Perseus
sandals_of_perseus.unidentified_name: a pair of worn fisherman's sandals with bronze buckles
sandals_of_perseus.lore: The sea washed Perseus and his mother ashore in a wooden chest upon the isle of Seriphos, and he grew up in a fisherman's house. At a feast he boasted that he would bring the king the Gorgon's head, and the king held him to his word. These plain sandals of leather with buckles of bronze were on his feet when he set out, for the winged pair was lent him later, and he had walked the first part of his road before ever the gods lent him anything.

kilt_of_the_pharaoh.name: Kilt of the Pharaoh
kilt_of_the_pharaoh.unidentified_name: a pleated linen kilt shot with gilt thread
kilt_of_the_pharaoh.lore: For three thousand years the shendyt was the kilt of Egypt's kings, fine linen wrapped about the hips and sharply pleated, with a tapering panel before, and sculptors carved it upon every pharaoh from the builders of the pyramids to the line of Cleopatra. In the tomb of Tutankhamun Howard Carter found heaped linen as dry as paper, kilts and tunics and more than a hundred loincloths, for a king was buried with such raiment as he meant to need again. Thus what is lost by one who dies in this kilt is not lost for good.
kilt_of_the_pharaoh.special: If you die wearing it, one thing you wore is kept whole in your grave for whoever finds it.

scale_of_dilmun.name: Scale of Dilmun
scale_of_dilmun.unidentified_name: a bronze scale shirt, green at the edges, smelling of salt
scale_of_dilmun.lore: Dilmun, as the folk of Sumer told, was a pure bright land in the sea toward the sunrise, where no raven croaked and no lion killed. It was without sweet water until the god Enki called up springs from under the earth, and there after the flood the gods gave a home to Ziusudra, the one man whom they suffered to live forever. Most scholars hold that it was the isle of Bahrain, where fresh springs yet rise through the salt sea, and this shirt of bronze is at home wherever water stands.
scale_of_dilmun.special: Beside water or a fountain, armor improves by 2 and you heal 1 health a turn.

helm_of_gilgamesh.name: Helm of Gilgamesh
helm_of_gilgamesh.unidentified_name: a beaten gold war helm shaped like braided hair
helm_of_gilgamesh.lore: Gilgamesh is given a reign at Uruk in the Sumerian King List, and his epic was old before Babylon was great. Near his city, in the Royal Cemetery of Ur, Leonard Woolley dug in the 1920s and lifted out a helmet beaten from one sheet of golden alloy in the likeness of a wig, with every curl and the knot behind chased in the metal. It had belonged to a man named Meskalamdug. The helm of a king looks for tribute, and gold that is offered to it is never wasted.
helm_of_gilgamesh.special: Once a floor, a power pays a thinking creature in sight to stand aside.

sandals_of_theseus.name: Sandals of Theseus
sandals_of_theseus.unidentified_name: a pair of weathered leather sandals with bronze studs
sandals_of_theseus.lore: Beneath a boulder at Troezen King Aegeus hid a sword and a pair of sandals, saying to the mother that the boy might come to Athens when he could lift it. Theseus lifted it at sixteen and went by land, which was the road of danger. There he bent Sinis between that robber's own pine trees, kicked Sciron from his own cliff and fitted Procrustes to his own iron bed. The sandals learned their lesson upon that road, and they give back harm to the doer in the same shape in which it came.
sandals_of_theseus.special: When a monster hits you, 1 time in 5 an ailment you are suffering passes to it.

greaves_of_qin.name: Greaves of the Qin Guard
greaves_of_qin.unidentified_name: a pair of lacquered leather greaves stamped with seal script
greaves_of_qin.lore: An army of fired clay was set to guard the First Emperor of Qin when he was buried in 210 BC, some eight thousand soldiers with no two faces alike, drawn up for battle in pits a mile from his tomb, and there farmers found them in 1974 as they dug a well. The sculptors had copied true armour plate by plate, in little squares of lacquered leather laced with cord. Lacquer sheds water and hardens the hide beneath, so that very little can eat through it, and the seal on these greaves names the foreman of the workshop.

cloak_of_odin.name: Wanderer's Cloak of Odin
cloak_of_odin.unidentified_name: a deep blue traveler's cloak with one missing eyelet
cloak_of_odin.lore: For a drink of wisdom Odin left one of his eyes in Mimir's well, and afterward he went through the world as an old man in a blue cloak, his hat pulled low upon that side. Grimnir he called himself, or Gangleri, or Vegtam. He would beg a seat by the fire and match riddles with kings and giants, and be gone before any thought to count his eyes, while each morning his ravens Huginn and Muninn brought him tidings. His cloak has the same hunger to know the nature of all things.

bracers_of_arjuna.name: Bracers of Arjuna
bracers_of_arjuna.unidentified_name: a pair of engraved leather archer's bracers with brass studs
bracers_of_arjuna.lore: Arjuna was the finest archer of the five Pandava brothers and could draw the bow Gandiva with either hand, yet on the morning of Kurukshetra, when he saw his teachers and kinsmen in the line against him, the bow slipped from his fingers. Krishna was his charioteer. What Krishna said to him between the waiting armies fills eighteen chapters, which are called the Bhagavad Gita, and when it was said Arjuna took up the bow again. In each new place the first arrow that the wearer looses flies with a mind thus settled.
bracers_of_arjuna.special: Your first shot on each floor hits half again as hard.

girdle_of_hippolyta.name: Girdle of Hippolyta
girdle_of_hippolyta.unidentified_name: a braided leather war-girdle with a bronze clasp
girdle_of_hippolyta.lore: Hippolyta, queen of the Amazons, had from her father Ares a war belt in token of her command. As his ninth Labour Heracles was sent to fetch it for a princess of Mycenae, and she came down to his ship and offered it freely. But Hera ran through the camp in the shape of an Amazon, crying that the stranger was stealing away the queen, and when the riders charged, Heracles believed himself betrayed and slew her. Her girdle answers still to any charge that runs straight and gathers as it goes.
girdle_of_hippolyta.special: After four steps in a straight line, your next blow hits half again as hard.

helm_of_leonidas.name: Helm of Leonidas
helm_of_leonidas.unidentified_name: a Corinthian bronze helm with a crest set ear to ear
helm_of_leonidas.lore: A rider whom the Persians sent to spy upon Thermopylae found the Spartans stripped for exercise and combing their long hair. Xerxes laughed at the report, but an exiled king of Sparta in his camp told him that these men dressed their hair when they meant to hazard their lives. For two days Leonidas held the pass, and on the third he sent most of his allies home and died with his three hundred, and his helm does its best work when the one who wears it is nearly spent.
helm_of_leonidas.special: When you are badly hurt, your blows land 15% harder.

cloak_of_mulan.name: Cloak of Mulan
cloak_of_mulan.unidentified_name: a heavy red wool cloak with frost-line patterns
cloak_of_mulan.lore: When the Khan's scroll of summons bore her father's name and he had no grown son, Mulan bought a horse in the east market, a saddle in the west, a bridle in the south and a whip in the north, and rode in his stead through ten years of war on the frontier. So sings the Ballad of Mulan from the age of the Northern Wei, and her comrades did not know her when they saw her in a dress. Upon holy ground this cloak lets the wearer put off the soldier and rest.
cloak_of_mulan.special: Once a floor, stepping onto an altar restores you completely.

haramaki_of_yoshitsune.name: Haramaki of Yoshitsune
haramaki_of_yoshitsune.unidentified_name: a cuirass of small lacquered plates laced with dark red silk
haramaki_of_yoshitsune.lore: Minamoto no Yoshitsune came in 1184 against the Taira fortress of Ichi-no-Tani, which had the sea before it and a cliff behind. He watched the deer picking their way down the cliff and judged that where a deer went a horse might follow, and with a handful of riders he plunged straight down upon the rear of the camp. A year later he destroyed the Taira fleet at Dan-no-ura, but his brother the shogun grew afraid of him and hunted him to death. His armour quickens still at every descent.
haramaki_of_yoshitsune.special: Hasted for 5 turns each time you go down a stair. Blessed while worn.

boots_of_thor.name: Iron Boots of Thor
boots_of_thor.unidentified_name: a pair of heavy iron boots scarred by lightning
boots_of_thor.lore: Three treasures of Thor are numbered by Snorri, the hammer, the belt of strength and the iron gloves with which he gripped the hammer, and no poet speaks of his boots. Yet Thor alone of the gods might not ride the rainbow bridge, lest it burn beneath him, and he waded four rivers daily to reach the seat of judgment by the World Tree, and forded Vimur while a giantess swelled the flood. The boots upon his feet bore him through all those waters, and sparks leap from them when enemies crowd close.
boots_of_thor.special: Each turn, 1 chance in 20 that lightning takes a twentieth of the health of a monster beside you.

helm_of_aragorn.name: Helm of the King Returned
helm_of_aragorn.unidentified_name: a winged silver helm with a pale gem in the brow
helm_of_aragorn.lore: The crown of Gondor, as Tolkien describes it, was a tall white helm with wings like a gull's of pearl and silver and seven gems in the circlet, and it waited in the tomb of a king through the long rule of the stewards. He who came to claim it had passed most of his life as a ranger who was called Strider. That he might reach his city in time he took the Paths of the Dead and summoned an army of oathbreakers to keep their word at last, and still the dead will listen to this helm.

robes_of_solomon.name: Robes of Solomon
robes_of_solomon.unidentified_name: a robe of gold thread embroidered with rows of strange names
robes_of_solomon.lore: Solomon asked for wisdom when God offered him whatever he would, and wealth and length of reign were given to him besides. Later tradition gave him also a signet ring that commanded the demons, and it was said that the names broidered upon his robes were theirs. The Temple that he built was twice destroyed, but the writings of Wisdom that bear his name have endured, and these robes are that same wisdom arrayed for the throne room.

armor_of_ragnarok.name: Armor of Ragnarök
armor_of_ragnarok.unidentified_name: an iron-and-bone harness scarred by old burns
armor_of_ragnarok.lore: Ragnarök is the doom of the gods, when Odin shall die in the wolf's mouth and Thor shall slay the world-serpent and walk nine steps before he falls by its venom. The world shall burn and sink, and rise again with fewer gods and a memory of what befell. This is the harness for that day, which the gods knew was coming and yet would go out to meet, and the Norse named this courage and would not call it despair.

crown_of_brahma.name: Crown of Brahma
crown_of_brahma.unidentified_name: a four-tiered golden crown that hums with mantra
crown_of_brahma.lore: Brahma woke upon a lotus that grew from the navel of sleeping Vishnu, and out of his thought came the worlds. The Puranas tell that he put forth a face for each quarter of the sky, that nothing he had made might pass from his sight, and that from his four mouths proceeded the four Vedas. He rides a white goose and bears a water pot and a string of prayer beads, and never a weapon. His crown has a tier for each of the faces, so that its wearer is not easily approached from behind.

duck_of_doom.name: Duck of Doom
duck_of_doom.lore: You should know better than to pick up a duck in a dungeon.

cestus_of_polydeuces.name: Cestus of Polydeuces
cestus_of_polydeuces.unidentified_name: a pair of ox-hide straps wound for the knuckles
cestus_of_polydeuces.lore: None among the Greeks could box so well as Polydeuces, who sailed with Jason in the Argo. When the ship put in among the Bebryces their king Amycus would let no stranger depart unless he boxed with him, and no stranger had ever won, but Polydeuces bound his fists with straps of ox-hide, let the bigger man grow weary and felled him with one blow above the ear. A boxer learns before all else how to endure a blow, and so will the wearer of these straps.

gloves_of_wayland.name: Wayland's Forge Gloves
gloves_of_wayland.unidentified_name: a pair of scorched leather gloves that smell of charcoal
gloves_of_wayland.lore: The finest smith in all the tales of the North was Wayland. King Nidud, who coveted his work and feared his freedom, cut the sinews behind his knees and set him upon an island to labour at the forge, but he who could not walk away made himself wings, one feather after another, and flew. Hands that have wrought so patiently under guard will not tremble when time runs short.

glove_of_tyr.name: Glove of Tyr
glove_of_tyr.unidentified_name: a single left-hand war glove; there was never a right
glove_of_tyr.lore: Fenrir the wolf would not suffer the ribbon Gleipnir near him unless one of the gods laid a hand between his jaws as a pledge of good faith. All of them knew that the pledge was false, and Tyr alone stepped forward. When the ribbon held, the wolf bit, and Tyr was one-handed ever after. It is by him that men swore their oaths, and this is the glove of the hand that was left to him.

jarngreipr_gauntlets.name: Jarngreipr
jarngreipr_gauntlets.unidentified_name: a pair of iron gauntlets too heavy for their size
jarngreipr_gauntlets.lore: Jarngreipr, which is to say the iron grippers, are counted by Snorri among three treasures of Thor, along with the hammer Mjolnir and the belt that doubles his strength. When the dwarves forged the hammer Loki took the shape of a fly and bit the one who worked the bellows, so that the handle came out too short and Thor cannot swing it without these gloves. A grip does not slip in them, and a blow carries somewhat further than it should.

bracers_of_atalanta.name: Bracers of Atalanta
bracers_of_atalanta.unidentified_name: a pair of light leather bracers scuffed by brambles
bracers_of_atalanta.lore: Atalanta was left upon a hillside by a father who had wished for a son, and a she-bear nursed her and hunters brought her up. She would marry only the man who could outrun her, and of the many who tried one won, by rolling three golden apples in her path. When the Calydonian Boar was hunted it was she who drew first blood, though a band of heroes could not, and in all that hunt there was nothing that could lay a hand on her.

vambraces_of_roland.name: Vambraces of Roland
vambraces_of_roland.unidentified_name: a pair of dented steel arm-guards with a Frankish cross
vambraces_of_roland.lore: Roland had command of the rear guard in 778, when Charlemagne's army marched homeward out of Spain through the pass of Roncevaux. The Song of Roland tells that three times his friend Oliver begged him to sound the horn and call back the king, and three times his pride refused. When none was left to save he blew at last, so hard that his temples burst. The rear guard held the pass to the last man, and to the end the arms that bore these vambraces did not drop.

vambraces_of_the_first_winter.name: Vambraces of the First Winter
vambraces_of_the_first_winter.unidentified_name: a pair of arm-guards of blue ice that does not melt
vambraces_of_the_first_winter.lore: Before ever there was earth or sky there was a great gap, with fire to the south and ice to the north, and where the two met the ice dripped and the drops became the giant Ymir. Odin and his brothers slew him and built the world out of his body. The creature that bore these vambraces claims to be older than that slaying, and the ice in them is of the first morning, so that no cold since then has had any power to harm them.

hair_shirt_of_becket.name: Becket's Hair Shirt
hair_shirt_of_becket.unidentified_name: a rough undershirt of goat hair
hair_shirt_of_becket.lore: Thomas Becket was friend and chancellor to the king, and loved fine raiment and good food. Henry II made him Archbishop of Canterbury, looking to have an ally there, but Becket took the part of the Church. On 29 December 1170 four of the king's knights cut him down in his own cathedral, and when the monks came to unclothe the body they found beneath the robes this shirt of coarse hair, which he had long worn against his skin where none could see it.

shirt_of_aslaug.name: Aslaug's Shirt
shirt_of_aslaug.unidentified_name: a grey shirt woven without a single seam showing
shirt_of_aslaug.lore: Aslaug, the daughter of Sigurd the dragon-slayer, was wife to Ragnar Lodbrok. When he would sail for England against her counsel she gave him a shirt of her own weaving and told him that no blade would bite him while he wore it. King Aella's men could not wound him, and when they cast him into a pit of serpents the snakes also would not touch him, until Aella had the shirt stripped from his back.

seamless_tunic.name: The Seamless Tunic
seamless_tunic.unidentified_name: a plain tunic woven in one piece from the top down
seamless_tunic.lore: The soldiers at the cross, as John's gospel tells, parted the clothes of Jesus into four shares, one to each, and the tunic remained. It was without seam, being woven in one piece from the top down, and when they had looked upon it they said, let us not tear it, and threw dice for it instead. So four hard men, with a day's killing behind them, agreed that this one thing should stay whole.

half_cloak_of_martin.name: Martin's Half Cloak
half_cloak_of_martin.unidentified_name: half of a red soldier's cloak, cut clean with a blade
half_cloak_of_martin.lore: As a young horseman of Rome at Amiens, Martin met upon a winter's day a beggar at the city gate who had scarcely any clothing. Having no money left, he drew his sword, cut his army cloak in two and gave the man the half. The other half the Frankish kings afterward kept as their holiest relic, and as its Latin name was cappa, its keepers were the cappellani and the room where it hung was the cappella, from which all chaplains and chapels have their names.

anansi_web_cloak.name: Anansi's Web Cloak
anansi_web_cloak.unidentified_name: a cloak of gold thread stitched all over with a pattern of spider web
anansi_web_cloak.lore: All stories belonged once to Nyame the sky god, as the Akan people of West Africa tell, until Anansi the spider sought to buy them. Nyame named a price that none could pay, the hornets, the python and the leopard, all alive, but Anansi, who was small and weak, tricked each of them into binding itself. From that day every story is a spider story, and it is the teller of the tale who decides how it shall end.
anansi_web_cloak.special: Once a floor, a blow that would take a quarter of your health leaves only a scratch.

arachne_silk_cloak.name: Arachne's Silk Cloak
arachne_silk_cloak.unidentified_name: a pale cloak of silk too fine to have been spun by hand
arachne_silk_cloak.lore: So well did Arachne of Lydia weave that the nymphs forsook their rivers to watch her, and she boasted that not Athena herself could teach her anything. The goddess came and wove beside her and, as Ovid tells, could find no fault in the girl's work, and tore it up for that very cause. Arachne was turned into a spider and has been weaving ever since, and whatever touches her thread is not soon free of it.
arachne_silk_cloak.special: A monster that strikes you hand to hand is slowed for 3 turns.

erlking_mantle.name: Mantle of the Erlking
erlking_mantle.unidentified_name: a mantle the green-grey of alder bark, cold to the touch
erlking_mantle.lore: Homeward through the night wood rode a father with his sick son in his arms, as Goethe told it in a poem of 1782, and the boy cried that the Erlking was calling to him. The father heard nothing but wind in the dry leaves and saw nothing but mist and old willows, and he rode the harder, yet when he reached the yard the child was dead. The boy had heard all that moved in that wood, and whoever puts on the king's mantle will hear as much.
erlking_mantle.special: You sense every monster within 6 tiles, even through walls.

falcon_cloak_of_freyja.name: Freyja's Falcon Cloak
falcon_cloak_of_freyja.unidentified_name: a cloak of barred brown feathers that lifts in still air
falcon_cloak_of_freyja.lore: Freyja had a cloak of falcon's feathers in which the wearer might fly, though she seldom used it herself. Loki borrowed it twice: once to learn which giant had stolen the hammer of Thor, and once to bear the goddess Idunn home in the shape of a nut, with an eagle but a wingbeat behind him. Each time he outflew what hunted him, though only by a little.

mantle_of_muspelheim.name: Surtur's Ember Mantle
mantle_of_muspelheim.unidentified_name: a mantle that glows at the hem like a banked fire
mantle_of_muspelheim.lore: Since before the gods were, Surtur has stood upon the border of Muspelheim to await the horn that shall summon him to burn the world, and in so long a waiting he has grown well used to heat. His mantle holds it still, so that fire runs off the wearer as rain off a slate roof and the body wrapped in it is harder to hurt by any means.

breeches_of_ragnar.name: Ragnar's Shaggy Breeches
breeches_of_ragnar.unidentified_name: a pair of shaggy breeches stiff with old pitch
breeches_of_ragnar.lore: A great serpent lay coiled about the house of a jarl's daughter, and her father promised her to the one who should kill it. Young Ragnar had shaggy breeches and a cloak made, boiled them in pitch and rolled in sand until they set hard, and the venom ran off them. So he won the princess, and a name to bear all his life, for Lodbrok means Shaggy Breeches.

greaves_of_goliath.name: Greaves of Goliath
greaves_of_goliath.unidentified_name: a pair of bronze greaves made for a man nine feet tall
greaves_of_goliath.lore: Goliath went out to war in a helmet of bronze and a coat of mail that weighed five thousand shekels, with bronze greaves upon his legs and a shield-bearer before him, as the first book of Samuel reckons it piece by piece. For forty days no soldier of Israel would face him, until David, a shepherd boy, refused all armour and brought a sling. These greaves served him faultlessly, but they could not guard his forehead, where the stone struck him.

nidhoggr_scale.name: Nidhoggr's Scale
nidhoggr_scale.unidentified_name: a single dark green scale as wide as a cloak
nidhoggr_scale.lore: Beneath the world-tree Yggdrasil the dragon Nidhoggr lies gnawing at the root. An eagle sits in the topmost boughs, and all day a squirrel named Ratatosk runs up and down the trunk bearing insults from the one to the other. The dragon has chewed there since the world began, amid the wet and rot at the bottom of all things, and nothing in that place has ever eaten into his hide.

serpent_scale_mail.name: Serpent Scale Mail
serpent_scale_mail.unidentified_name: a coat of green scales, each one the size of a hand
serpent_scale_mail.lore: Of the three children of Loki one was the serpent Jormungandr, which Odin flung into the sea that rings the world, and there it grew until it could circle the earth and take its own tail in its mouth. Thor hooked it once with an ox head for bait and hauled until his feet broke through the bottom of the boat, and by its venom he shall die at the last. These scales were taken from a young one, and there is no poison that can pass through them.

green_girdle.name: The Green Girdle
green_girdle.unidentified_name: a belt of green silk worked with gold thread
green_girdle.lore: Sir Gawain was bound to take upon his bare neck one stroke of the Green Knight's axe. On the night before, his host's wife offered him a girdle of green silk, saying that no man who wore it could be killed, and he took it and told no one. The axe came down and did but nick him, and then the Green Knight laughed, named the girdle and forgave him. Gawain wore it home for a mark of his shame, and all the Round Table put on green to share it with him.
green_girdle.special: Once a floor, a blow that would take a quarter of your health leaves only a scratch.

bloomleaf_cloak.name: Bloomleaf Cloak
bloomleaf_cloak.unidentified_name: a cloak of broad green leaves
bloomleaf_cloak.lore: As a Bloomsaur grows it sheds broad waxen leaves, cupped so that the rain rolls from them in beads. The leaves of this cloak are still living, and are stitched at the stems with twists of grass, but their ragged edges show that they were never shed, for they were torn from the back of a young one. Beneath them the drip of the deep shafts never comes to iron, and nothing you wear will rust while the cloak is on you.
bloomleaf_cloak.special: Nothing you wear rusts while it is on you: not a rust trap's water, not a rust monster's feelers.
bloomleaf_cloak._design_note: Winning-build plan 2026-11-13 section 3.8. Worn and dropped by Old Nickel (data/monsters.json old_nickel, unique_drop_id), placed every run on one floor from 1 to the Emberpup's (src/emberpup_encounter.py). It starts unidentified in the data like every unique, and drops identified (special_properties.arrives_known: Game._spawn_unique_item grants it known, as the Magic Dungeon Carrot arrives). rustproof_wearer is read by Player.is_rustproof (status_effects.rust_worn_gear). Only this cloak keeps the rain off the Emberpup. Traders refuse it (a scripted-only unique) and thieves skip it (items.withheld: is_unique). Light cloak guard, Vapourward by its lore (tools/content/unique_armor_ladder_2026_11.py PICKS).

calydonian_boar_hide.name: Hide of the Calydonian Boar
calydonian_boar_hide.unidentified_name: a coat of bristled black hide with a tusked hood
calydonian_boar_hide.special: Its bristles stand like spear shafts: a blade's cut glances off it.
calydonian_boar_hide.lore: When King Oeneus of Calydon forgot Artemis in the offerings of harvest, she sent upon him a boar bigger than a bull, with bristles like spear shafts and tusks like an elephant's, and half the heroes of Greece went out to hunt it. Atalanta drew first blood with an arrow and Meleager slew it with his spear and awarded her the hide and tusked head. His uncles took them from her, and for that he killed them. Pausanias beheld the hide rotting in Athena's temple at Tegea, and this is the same, as it was before the moths came.

brazen_hands_of_stheno.name: Brazen Hands of Stheno
brazen_hands_of_stheno.unidentified_name: a pair of clawed gauntlets of scaled bronze
brazen_hands_of_stheno.special: A gorgon's grip of bronze: they add to your Strength while you wear them.
brazen_hands_of_stheno.lore: Three Gorgons there were, as Apollodorus describes them, with the scales of serpents twined about their heads, tusks like a boar's, wings of gold and hands of bronze. Medusa alone was mortal, for Stheno and Euryale cannot die, and the name of Stheno signifies strength. These are her hands, or such as she left behind when she was struck down, scaled in bronze and clawed at every finger, and they give to whoever wears them a gorgon's grip.

crones_burial_veil.name: The Crone's Burial Veil
crones_burial_veil.unidentified_name: a hooded veil of old grey linen
crones_burial_veil.special: She heard her own death foretold every night in the grave: no gaze and no terror takes hold of whoever wears it.
crones_burial_veil.lore: A fortune-teller once told the folk of a market town too plainly which child would not see the spring and which husband would not come home, and they buried her alive in this veil. She whispered on in the darkness until the dead whispered back, and every one of them heard his own death foretold in her voice, with the day and the hour. Her own she heard every night for years, until she had no fear left of anything, and that fearlessness the veil remembers.
